grounding.states: large eggs dropped into boiling water: about 12 minutes gives a fully set yolk
grounding.from: Healthline says 12 to 13 minutes gives fully hard-boiled eggs that are not over-cooked

grounding.states: 10 minutes gives a firm yolk that may be slightly soft in the center
grounding.from: At 10 minutes, the eggs are mostly cooked through but slightly soft in the center

grounding.states: past about 14 to 15 minutes the whites turn rubbery and the yolk dry
grounding.from: Past about 14–15 minutes the eggs turn rubbery or dry
smaller ones cook quicker while larger ones need extra time

value.answer: For large eggs dropped into boiling water, about 12 minutes gets you a fully set yolk. 10 minutes is firm but can be a bit soft in the middle, and past 14 or 15 minutes the whites go rubbery and the yolk gets dry. Smaller eggs cook a bit faster.
